title: test_root_verb_vocabulary compares a snapshot's relative path as posix, so its colliding-registration tooth holds on Windows
intention: test_root_verb_vocabulary's colliding-registration tooth compares a snapshot's relative path as posix, so it is green on Windows as on Linux: _snapshots returns each relative path via as_posix().
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendell, house checkout and a branch: test_a_colliding_registration_is_refused fails at test_root_verb_vocabulary.py:257 because _snapshots (line 171) returns str(p.relative_to(home)), which prints backslashes on Windows, against the posix literal [".cairn/devices/15d6-extender/0/last_known.json"]. The product is right; the proof assumed a separator.
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 9: a tooth that is red only on one platform's separator was never measuring the component; CP4 resolves the chafe.
how: In _snapshots, return p.relative_to(home).as_posix() instead of str(p.relative_to(home)); add PROVES for this ticket mapping clause 1 to test_a_colliding_registration_is_refused. Confirm the whole file green on Windows.

clauses.claim: test_a_colliding_registration_is_refused is green on Windows and on posix, where on Windows it reds at line 257 because _snapshots returned backslash relative paths

decisions.text: D1: _snapshots returns as_posix() relative paths; the tooth is the existing one, red at HEAD on Windows.

measured.saw: test_root_verb_vocabulary.py::test_a_colliding_registration_is_refused fails at line 257 on Windows: AssertionError: ['.cairn\\devices\\15d6-extender\\0\\last_known.json'], in the untouched house checkout and on a branch alike; _snapshots at line 171 is str(p.relative_to(home)); the other uses are `not _snapshots(home)`.
measured.how: bin/cairn test cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_root_verb_vocabulary.py in the house checkout and in a worktree; read lines 171-172 and 249-257
